data.long_meaning: Ahlad is a Sanskrit name derived from the word ‘ahlād’, meaning ‘happy’ or ‘blissful’. It is believed that the name Ahlad bestows happiness and contentment upon its bearer.

Hindu traditions place a great emphasis on the emotional wellbeing and happiness of individuals. The name Ahlad symbolizes the desire and expectation for bliss, happiness, and joy in one's life. It is also a reminder for its bearer to spread happiness and positivity to those around them.

historical_references.reference: Ahlad was a king of the Vakataka dynasty in India, who ruled from approximately 460 to 495 AD. He is best known for his patronage of the arts and architecture, particularly the rock-cut temples at Ajanta and Ellora.
historical_references.context: An inscription at the Ajanta Caves identifies Ahlad as the patron of the caves, which were created during his reign. The temples at Ellora, which are also attributed to Ahlad's reign, showcase the artistic and architectural achievements of the time.

historical_references.reference: Ahlad was also a famed Hindu philosopher and scholar, who lived in the 12th century AD. He is best known for his commentary on the Bhagavad Gita, titled 'The Gitasara'. This work is considered a seminal text in the development of the Bhakti Movement in India, which emphasized the importance of devotion to God as a means to spiritual growth.
historical_references.context: Ahlad's commentary on the Bhagavad Gita is considered a major contribution to Hindu theology, particularly in the development of the Bhakti Movement. His work was influential in shaping the perspective of many Hindu philosophers and scholars who came after him.
